t: Shift registers: tracking parts down a line
html:
The bottle line’s central idea is older than PLCs: an indexing conveyor moves a fixed pitch and stops; a sensor at the head reads what arrived; and a shift register, one bit per stop, moves what it knows one place down the line each time the belt steps. Bit 0 is the stop at the sensor; bit n is n stops downstream. A station at stop 12 reads bit 12 and knows what is standing in front of it without a sensor of its own.

BSL(array,control,source_bit,length) (Bit Shift Left) does the move. Every time the rung goes true it shifts the whole array up one bit, copies the source bit into bit 0, and reports the bit that fell off the far end in control.UL. BSR shifts the other way. The control tag is a CONTROL; the length is the number of bits in use.

XIC(Dwell.DN)[BSL(Exist[0],Exist_Ctl,LS1,48),BSL(Large[0],Large_Ctl,LS2,48),BSL(Broken[0],Broken_Ctl,LS3,48),BSL(Reject[0],Reject_Ctl,Cam_Bad,48)];

Four registers, four questions about every stop: is there a bottle (Exist, from LS1), is it large (Large, from LS2, a retro beam set at a height only a large bottle breaks), is it broken (Broken, from LS3, a diffuse eye that only reports broken bottles), and did the camera reject it (Reject, from Cam_Bad, step 15). Downstream, a station asks its question with one XIC.

Which bit is my station?

Count the stops. The belt indexes 40 px. The head sensors sit on the stop grid at x = 160, 200 and 240, one stop apart, and the stations at 440 (filler), 560 (capper), 600 (labeler), 720 (scrap gate) and 1000 (divert gate). The scrap gate is (720 − 240) / 40 = 12 stops past LS3. So Broken[0].12… almost.

The frame: before or after the shift

The shift happens at the end of the dwell, just before the belt steps. During the dwell, while the bottles stand still, the register was last shifted before the previous step: bit n describes the bottle that is now at stop n + 1. A rung that runs during the dwell (the gates in step 8, on Dwell.TT) therefore reads one bit lower than the count: Broken[0].11 for the scrap gate. A rung that runs after the shift and before the step (the fill, cap and label requests in steps 5, 7 and 10, which wait on Dwell.DN) reads the count itself. The table every lesson in Part IV refers to:

Each cell is “during the dwell · after the shift”, and bold is the frame the station’s rung actually uses (the filler, for example, reads Exist[0].7 and Broken[0].5). The Reject register starts at the camera, not at the head, so its bits are counted from there: bit 0 at the scrap gate, bit 7 at the divert gate. These numbers are not assumed: the program’s test suite runs the line and checks every bit against the bottle standing at each station, and the comments in the routines say which frame they are in.

Watch for

A sensor that is not on the stop grid sees the same bottle at two stops, and a broken bottle then occupies two bits of the Broken register: the scrap gate fires twice and the good bottle behind the broken one goes into the shredder. The head sensors in the template sit at 160, 200 and 240 for this reason; if you move one, re-measure your bits with Monitor Tags and a slow belt.
